title: RLS test coverage ratio
notes: Ratio = policy-bearing tables (parsed from every `CREATE POLICY ... ON "visionquest"."<Table>"` across prisma/migrations, deduped) that have at least one POSITIVE and one NEGATIVE case in src/lib/rls.test.ts, over all policy-bearing tables. See scripts/bench/suites/lib/rls-parse.mjs's header for the exact positive/negative heuristic and its known limitation (whole-block attribution: a table counts as covered if ANY of its attributed it() blocks shows positive evidence and ANY shows negative evidence, not necessarily the SAME block). HISTORY. 2026-09-05, at this suite's promotion: 18/92 = 0.1956, floored DOWN to 0.15 per 'first measure it, never 0.90 by default'. `Message`, `SpokesRecord` and `Certification` genuinely had ZERO `tx.<model>.` references in the suite despite each having a CREATE POLICY — flagged then as very likely the single most actionable finding of that promotion. 2026-09-07 (ticket D6): closed. The suite now covers 93 of 93 policy-bearing tables — every one of the 74 that had no pair got one positive case (the role the policy admits reads the row it owns or manages, and NOT the neighbouring row it does not) and one negative (the excluded role reads zero rows where the exclusion is a USING clause, or is refused with 42501 where it is a WITH CHECK clause), written against the policies actually installed in Postgres (pg_policies), not against a migration file, and verified by executing them on a migrated database rather than a `db push` schema. Ratio 1.0, so the floor is 1.0 with tolerance 0 and rises no further: a NEW table that gains a CREATE POLICY without gaining a positive and a negative case reds this gate on the PR that adds it, which is the point. Two facts about that gate worth knowing before touching it. (1) It is a STATIC parse — it reads the migrations and the test source and needs no database, so it runs in CI wherever `bench --tier=gate` runs, including where RLS_TEST_ENABLED is unset and the suite itself is skipped. Coverage being 1.0 therefore does NOT mean the 252 cases passed; it means they exist and are attributable. The cases themselves are proven by `npm run test:rls` against a real Postgres. (2) Because attribution is by `tx.<model>.`/`prisma.<model>.` reference, a case written with a computed delegate (`tx[name]`) counts for nothing — write the delegate literally. Raising this floor is not possible and lowering it is not allowed; the way to change the number is to add or remove a policy.
